paragraphs.source_en:
Words for Music Perhaps: many of the poems in The Winding Stair and Other Poems
had been included in Words for Music Perhaps (1932). See Yeats's note on The
Winding Stair and Other Poems, pp. 461-2.
 268-74: Crazy Jane is a fictitious character, based in part on "Cracked Mary,"
a woman who lived near Gort in County Galway.
 268.5: "Jack the Journeyman" is a fictitious character.
 269.5: in Greek mythology, Europa, daughter of Aegnor, king ofTyre, is carried
off by the god Zeus, who comes to her in the form of a bull.
 270: in Christianity, the Day of Judgment is the apocalypse, when the good and
evil are judged and sent to either heaven or hell.
 274.18: Irish trtiithnln, a blade of grass.
 28o.8: according to legend, the hair of Berenice II (ca. 273-221 B.c.), offered
for the safe return of her husband Ptolemy III (ca. 284-221 B.c.), king of
Egypt, became a constellation, Coma Berenices.
 281.1: in Plato's Republic, the universe revolves on the "spindle of Necessity."
